reports.rendered_content: Implementation of the graybox coverage algorithm includes 17 coverage-engine files, a worker, UI, and tests, with both joint and fixed-first search modes. Joint mode evaluates all legal coarse pairs ranked by bitset union before applying quality/contribution tie-breakers, avoiding premature discard of complementary origins. Correctness verdict: Algorithm architecture 8/10, search modes 7.5/10, readiness for complex imported sets 4/10. Surface sampler is deterministic, sampling triangles proportionally to world-space area via barycentric coordinates. Origin evaluation includes segment occlusion, geometric face normals, viewing angle, approximate projected texel density, separate visibility/usable-coverage bitsets, and continuous quality values. Shared engine uses 4,096 coarse samples, 256 candidates, retained pair seeds, 24,576 fine samples, local offsets, and separate fixed-first/joint branches. Tests cover deterministic sampling, double-sided occlusion, marginal second-origin ranking, non-greedy pair ranking, candidate generation, and both search modes. Two blockers remain: (1) imported sets can produce zero legal candidates because candidate clearance uses object AABBs rather than actual geometry, causing origins inside large AABBs (e.g., room shells) to be rejected; fix requires triangle-level clearance via BVH point-to-triangle distance or shapecast, plus regression test; (2) geometry representation will not scale to heavy imports due to per-triangle expansion.
